officialTitle: Vinorelbine plus Cisplatin vs. Observation in Resected Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 482 patients underwent randomization to vinorelbine plus cisplatin (242 patients) or observation (240)

clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant vinorelbine plus cisplatin prolong survival after complete resection of stage IB or II NSCLC?

pico.population: Completely resected stage IB or II NSCLC with good performance status
pico.outcomes: Primary: OS. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, toxicity

publications.title: Vinorelbine plus cisplatin vs. observation in resected non-small-cell lung cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Overall survival was significantly prolonged in the chemotherapy group as compared with the observation group (94 vs. 73 months; hazard ratio for death, 0.69; P=0.04)
as was relapse-free survival (not reached vs. 46.7 months; hazard ratio for recurrence, 0.60; P<0.001)
Five-year survival rates were 69 percent and 54 percent, respectively (P=0.03).

safety.description: Neutropenia (any grade) and grade 3 febrile neutropenia with chemotherapy
safety.sourceQuote: Chemotherapy caused neutropenia in 88 percent of patients (including grade 3 febrile neutropenia in 7 percent)

safety.description: Deaths from toxic effects of chemotherapy
safety.sourceQuote: death from toxic effects in two patients (0.8 percent)

strengths: Randomised with OS as primary endpoint

clinicalImplications.text: Supported adjuvant vinorelbine–cisplatin as a standard regimen after resection of stage II NSCLC; the benefit in stage IB was later questioned in pooled analyses.

tumourBoardPearl.text: JBR.10 is the reference trial for vinorelbine–cisplatin in resected stage IB–II disease; neutropenia is the dominant toxicity.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 15972865. 95% CIs not reported in the abstract and therefore omitted.
